findings.note: Age comes from plain arithmetic on SAS day counts (&as_of minus date_of_birth, divided by 365.25). In Spark, date_of_birth is a DATE and as_of must be turned into a date, so this needs datediff or date functions.

mean(x.paid) is mixed with ungrouped columns, so SAS remerges the mean over the rows the WHERE keeps (one line of business) back onto every row. Spark needs a window or a join to the per-line average of paid.

The %do loop writes one PROC SQL per line of business (MOT, HOM, TRV), and lines 79-83 union the results. In Spark this becomes a Python loop or a single query grouped by line of business, filtered to those three codes.
round(2.5*loss_ratio, 0.5) rounds to the nearest half, half away from zero, with fuzz. F.round takes decimal places, so this needs something like floor(x*2+0.5)/2 plus fuzz handling.
round(points*age_load*county_load, 0.01) is applied to a computed double. SAS's fuzz rounds near-half values up, but Spark's F.round on the binary value can round them down.
The first assignment, 'HIGH', fixes tier at length 4, so 'MEDIUM' is silently cut to 'MEDI' (the output schema has tier as char 4). Spark must reproduce 'MEDI' on purpose.
as_of_date is the number &as_of (a SAS day count) shown with yymmdd10. In Spark it must be converted from days since 1960-01-01 to a date.
